title: MR scroll & search pattern (sample series)
clinicalHistory: Teaching sample — no clinical scenario. Practice a systematic scroll through a short MR stack before opening real cases.
technique: Bundled pydicom emri_small sample (10 frames, offline).
primaryDiagnosis: Normal sample anatomy for orientation only.
learningObjectives: Scroll the stack smoothly without losing orientation.
Pause on a slice and describe what you see before advancing.
Use window/level presets appropriate to MR brain tissue.
discussion: This case uses the bundled offline MR series so every environment can teach scroll discipline without Orthanc. Treat it as a warm-up before DICOM-backed cases.
references: FlowRad bundled sample — pydicom emri_small (public domain teaching data).

findings.label: Start — mid stack
findings.description: Begin in the middle of the stack. Name the plane and set a default brain window before hunting for pathology.
teachingPoints: Always locate mid-slice before scrolling systematically.
Say your search pattern out loud — it becomes the script the AI tutor follows.

findings.label: Inferior sweep
findings.description: Scroll inferiorly through the remaining frames. Note how parenchymal contrast changes slice to slice.
teachingPoints: Scroll in one direction per pass — do not oscillate randomly.
If something catches your eye, stop and window before continuing.

findings.label: Superior sweep
findings.description: Return toward the superior slices. Compare symmetry left versus right on each stop.
teachingPoints: Compare paired structures on every slice — asymmetry is often the first clue.
Finish the pass at the top of the stack before calling the study complete.
